avertissement: Traductions automatiques des textes français ; chaque nombre a été vérifié contre le français. Les documents de la Ville sont en français et font foi.

canopee.description: Tree planting, greening, control of emerald ash borer and heat islands.
canopee.enBref: This year, the City is paying companies to plant and maintain trees on streets and in parks, and it is funding an organization that plants on private and institutional land. Boroughs are adding their own money, machinery and teams of employees to plant trees. Two boroughs have also allowed construction projects to depart from the rules on trees and greening.

etapes.titre: Contracts to plant trees on streets
etapes.texte: City council awards two contracts to 7574479 Canada inc. and Terrassement Technique Sylvain Labrecque inc. to supply and plant 1,374 trees on public land, then water, maintain and replace some of them. The authorized expense is $2,456,590.55, taxes included, and the trees go to seven boroughs, including Saint-Laurent (423), Verdun (281) and Pierrefonds-Roxboro (265).

etapes.titre: Money to plant on private properties
etapes.texte: The City is paying $3,071,550 to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain to plant and maintain trees on private and institutional sites from March 24 to December 31, 2026. The organization and the partners of the Alliance forêt urbaine must plant 14,500 trees and 2,500 shrubs in 2026.

Pierrefonds-Roxboro transfers up to $162,233.12 from its parks fund to buy trees and plants. Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve rents a mini backhoe loader with operator for $152,916.75 and sets aside $200,000 for additional blue-collar worker teams, with a target of about 1,000 trees planted in 2026.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve allows a company to expand its building at 1620, rue Préfontaine with 25 trees and 5% greening, instead of the required 40 trees and 25%, with the company compensating on its other properties. Montréal-Nord allows trees to be planted less than 1.5 metres from the street line at 5745, boulevard Léger, for a two-storey building.

etapes.titre: Work at parc Pratt, in Outremont
etapes.texte: Outremont awards URBEX CONSTRUCTION INC. the renovation of the parc Pratt chalet and the redevelopment of its surroundings, including planting of vegetation, water retention and new pathways. The authorized expense is $800,416.17, taxes included, financed mainly by the Programme de réfection et de verdissement des parcs locaux.

aSurveiller.texte: The Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain must submit progress reports on July 31 and October 31, 2026, its accountability report by December 31, 2026 at the latest, then its report and financial statements on March 31, 2027.
Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve's tree planting takes place from April or May to November 2026.
Watering, maintenance and replacement of trees planted under the central city contract continue until the end of November 2029.

deneigement.description: Snow removal and snow loading contracts, spreading of abrasives, parking by-laws.

etapes.texte: Several boroughs rented vacuum sweepers, tanker trucks, sidewalk washers and a mini sweeper with operator to remove abrasives in the spring. Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve authorized $574,920.99, taxes included, for four sweepers and three tanker trucks in 2026 and 2027 [CA26 27 0008].

etapes.titre: Snow removal at downtown public squares
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie awarded companies the maintenance, cleanliness and snow removal of Square Viger, Place des Montréalaises and six other public squares, including square Dorchester and square Victoria. The borough also extended snow removal for the Quartier des Spectacles by one year, until April 1, 2027 [CA26 24 0067].

etapes.titre: Additional funding and staff for the 2025-2026 season
etapes.texte: Montréal-Nord paid an extra $106,150.97 for renting an additional grader during the winter of 2025-2026 [CA26 10 086], and Saint-Léonard drew $200,000 from its surpluses for staff and the purchase of salt and sand [CA26 13 0121]. Verdun offered city council to itself provide staff for its snow disposal site.

etapes.titre: Extensions decided by the central city
etapes.texte: City council and the executive committee extended by 12 months the turnkey snow removal contracts of Anjou, Montréal-Nord and Pierrefonds-Roxboro, the towing contracts of four boroughs, equipment rental in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie and snow removal for a parking lot in Montréal-Est. The extension of the turnkey contracts costs $7,399,240.83, taxes included [CM26 0548].

Ville-Marie extended, for the winter of 2026-2027, the rental of tractor-loaders with operators and allocated $323,361.50 from its surpluses [CA26 240129]. Ahuntsic-Cartierville renewed the rental of a compact tractor loader and Anjou renewed the rental of a grader.

aSurveiller.texte: Saint-Léonard states that the adoption of its snow removal by-law is planned for September 8, 2026, with a notice of coming into force on September 9, 2026.
The extended towing contracts start on November 15, 2026.
The rental of equipment with operator in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie starts on November 1, 2026 and runs until March 31, 2027.
The rental of a grader in Anjou covers November 15, 2026 to April 15, 2027.
Snow removal for the parking lot of the Jacinthe-Fyfe building is extended from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2027.

eau-egouts.description: Pipes, drinking water production plants, Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, retention basins.
eau-egouts.enBref: This year, the City is borrowing to finance the disinfection plant at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant and new water mains in the Namur–De la Savane sector. It is awarding contracts to rehabilitate water pipes without trenching, rebuild streets along with their sewers and waterworks, and replace lead water service connections. It is also adding funds to projects already underway and purchasing the products and services needed to operate its plants.

etapes.texte: City council is awarding contracts to rehabilitate secondary water pipes by lining, a trenchless technique, and to redo pavement and sidewalks on streets in several boroughs. These contracts also include replacing lead water service connections, on both the public and private sides.

The City is adding money to contracts already awarded: $200,000 in contingencies for boulevard De Maisonneuve (CA26 240015) and $1,055,231.53 for the 750 mm pipe on rue Saint-Antoine Ouest (CG26 0153). It is also adding $12,144,522.14 in contingencies for the pipe on rue de la Cathédrale, after an inspection revealed more damaged sections than in 2019 (CG26 0336).

Contracts are being awarded to rebuild water pipes, sewers and roadways together, notably along rue Guy between Saint-Jacques and René-Lévesque, for a total expenditure of $28,921,033.25 (CG26 0245), and on rue De Champlain, where a 1,200 mm water main installed in 1927 is being replaced (CG26 0332). Other similar projects affect Saint-Laurent, Lachine, Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles and Pierrefonds-Roxboro.

etapes.titre: Plants, wastewater treatment plant and new loan
etapes.texte: The City is renewing support for the system that controls the processes at the Jean-R.-Marcotte plant, extending the purchase of polymers for this plant, adding aluminum sulphate for the Pointe-Claire drinking water production plant, and extending leak detection by probe in water mains. It is also adopting a $12,000,000 loan to build water mains between boulevard Cavendish and rue Isabella, in the Namur–De la Savane sector.

aSurveiller.texte: The pipe along autoroute 15 Nord and the Atwater ramp must be rehabilitated by no later than December 18, 2026.
Work on rue de la Cathédrale, up to the McTavish reservoir, must be completed by March 2027.
The rue Guy project must continue until December 2027.
Leak detection in water mains must be completed by June 2028.
The ozone plant at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant is expected to be commissioned in 2029.

frederic-back.titre: Parc Frédéric-Back and Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel
frederic-back.description: The former quarry turned dump, transformed into a park in phases: urban greenhouses, biogas capture, electrical system upgrade.
frederic-back.enBref: This year, the City is moving forward on three fronts at parc Frédéric-Back and the Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel: a greenhouse complex in the Saint-Michel neighbourhood, the modernization of electrical facilities linked to biogas capture, and park maintenance. It is also requesting financial assistance from Québec for an east-west pedestrian and cycling link with a footbridge. At the same time, the borough is redeveloping rue De Louvain, along the edge of the park.

etapes.titre: Request for assistance for the east-west link
etapes.texte: The City is asking the Ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable du Québec for assistance of up to $2,000,000 for a 900-metre trail crossing the park from east to west, including a footbridge of about 150 metres (CG26 0121). The project also includes rainwater management structures and a 12.7-hectare meadow.

The agglomeration approves the construction of a research, training and community production greenhouse complex, valued at $2,185,000, then delegates the project to city council (CG26 0124). The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension offers to carry it out and city council accepts (CA26 14 0039, CM26 0363).

The City awards Systèmes Urbains inc. a contract worth $1,091,693.37, taxes included, for the second phase of electrical work at the Complexe environnemental de Saint-Michel, which includes a new 25 kV power supply, a backup generator and an automated system to manage biogas capture (CG26 0223). It also entrusts two companies with the general maintenance and ecological and horticultural management of the park for 30 months (CG26 0224).

The borough entrusts Groupe MPotvin with the redevelopment of rue De Louvain, between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum amount of $8,199,514.82, taxes included, and authorizes a total expenditure of $11,192,464.62. The work covers sewers and waterworks, lighting, traffic lights, sidewalks, the bike path and plantings.

The City is extending by five months the rental of a compost screener and a loader tractor with operator at the Complexe environnemental de Saint-Michel, for $296,349.21 more, taxes included. The compost, made from leaves collected in parks and streets, is used in particular for the development of parc Frédéric-Back (CG26 0320).

The borough entrusts Les industries Harnois inc. with the supply and installation of the greenhouse complex, for a maximum amount of $499,865.92, taxes included, and authorizes a total expenditure of $574,845.80. The project involves two greenhouses with structure, envelope, natural ventilation, ground surfaces, interior partitions and condensation water management.

aSurveiller.texte: Greenhouses: delivery of infrastructure in July 2026, work starting in August 2026 and expected to finish in December 2026, according to the borough's file.
Greenhouses commissioning announced for winter 2027.
The call for projects under the Ministère des Transports' assistance program, for the footbridge and the east-west link, ends on November 26, 2026.
Rue De Louvain: work in three phases, from May to November 2026, from May to October 2027, then from May to August 2028.
Park maintenance: contracts from May 1, 2026 to October 31, 2028; 26 hectares will be added to the park in 2027 in the Boisé Ouest sector.
Rental of the screener and loader tractor from June 20 to October 15, 2026.

grand-parc-ouest.description: Canada's largest municipal park, being assembled: land acquisitions, Anse-à-l'Orme, Cap-Saint-Jacques, Bois-de-la-Roche, parc-nature des Sources.

etapes.titre: More money for the stone walls
etapes.texte: The City is adding $162,897.98 to the contract with Les Constructions H2D inc. to rebuild heritage walls along chemin de Senneville, bringing the contract to $1,174,331.77. According to the file, buried stones, surplus mortar and a deteriorated culvert explain the increase; the work, 60% complete as of December 1, 2025, resumes on May 15, 2026.

The City is submitting the application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector, described as covering 330 hectares, for DarkSky International's international Urban Night Sky Place designation. The application involves no spending; the City commits to producing a lighting management plan, bringing its light fixtures up to standard, and keeping the site accessible in the evening.

etapes.titre: Two sectors listed as natural environments
etapes.texte: The City is listing the parc-nature des Sources (38.32 ha) and the Anse-à-l'Orme sector of the Grand parc de l'Ouest (429 ha) in the Répertoire des milieux naturels protégés et contributifs à la biodiversité de l'agglomération, with conservation plans. It is also taking note of the 2025 report on the areas.

The City is awarding Gendron Gestion Civil inc. the contract to rebuild the culvert under chemin Senneville, as part of the modernization of the Bois-de-la-Roche agricultural hub, for a total expenditure of $481,850.45. The work includes the new culvert, roadway repairs and replacement of the safety guardrails.

aSurveiller.texte: Expected completion of work on the chemin de Senneville stone walls: July 10, 2026.
Submission of the Cap-Saint-Jacques lighting management plan: February 2027.
Response from DarkSky International on the designation: April 2027.

itinerance.description: Support for organizations, warming centres and shelters for people experiencing homelessness.
itinerance.enBref: The City lends municipal buildings free of charge to organizations so they can open warming centres, and it funds organizations that work with people experiencing homelessness. A Ville-Marie public works team carries out cleanliness interventions related to homelessness in other boroughs, which accept the offer one by one. The City is also adopting a framework to receive private cash donations intended for shelter and housing.

etapes.titre: Two buildings lent out for the winter
etapes.texte: The City is lending the former Sainte-Bibiane church, at 5600, 12e Avenue, free of charge to the Centre des Femmes de convictions de Montréal for a warming centre for women, from December 15, 2025 to April 30, 2026. It is also lending the former monastère des Recluses Missionnaires, at 12050, boulevard Gouin Est, to Projets Autochtones du Québec until April 30, 2026, and is transferring $97,000 from the Service de l'habitation to the Service de la gestion et de la planification des immeubles to cover building costs (CG26 0066).

etapes.titre: Warming centre at the Bain St-Denis
etapes.texte: The City is lending the former Bain St-Denis, at 7075, rue Saint-Hubert, free of charge to L'Amour en Action SYL DAN for a warming centre open from 4 p.m. to 8 a.m., seven days a week, for 90 days starting February 1, 2026. The value of the loan is estimated at $56,978 (CG26 0116).

etapes.titre: Contracts and outreach workers in the boroughs
etapes.texte: Verdun is paying $12,950 to the Société de développement social to keep two psychosocial outreach workers in its municipal facilities from January 5 to February 6, 2026. Ahuntsic-Cartierville is raising to $126,615.07, taxes included, the contract awarded to Les services de cohabitation sociale COHAB inc. to operate a warming centre during the winter of 2025-2026.

The City is granting $5,407,736 to 15 organizations and an additional $3,942,461 to 10 already-funded organizations, under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs 2026-2028, for projects ending December 31, 2028. The projects focus on the inclusion of people experiencing homelessness, cohabitation in public space, and awareness-raising.

City council is adopting a framework to receive private financial contributions intended for housing, shelter and social cohabitation: donors do not choose which project is funded, and the City may refuse a donation. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is transferring $250,000 from its surplus for improvement work on the temporary warming centre at the Bain Saint-Denis. City council is adopting a declaration of support for people experiencing homelessness and a motion from the Opposition officielle on a municipal rent support fund.

aSurveiller.texte: The agreement on the public works team accepted by Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles runs until May 15, 2027.
Financial support under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs ends on December 31, 2028.

logement.description: Grants, land and social, affordable or student housing projects, including those of the SHDM and the OMHM.
logement.enBref: The City approves the 2026 budgets of the SHDM and the Office municipal d'habitation de Montréal, transfers or purchases land for social housing and pays grants to organizations that build affordable housing. It also amends the by-law that requires developers to include social and affordable housing in their projects.

etapes.texte: City council approves the 2026 budget of the Société d'habitation et de développement de Montréal, which manages 393 buildings and more than 5,200 affordable housing units. The urban agglomeration council approves that of the Office municipal d'habitation de Montréal, which houses 42,587 households.

The City obtains from the Government of Canada, at no cost, half the rights to a 3,658.8 square-metre lot on rue Jolicoeur, in Pierrefonds-Roxboro. It also transfers, at no cost, to the Coopérative d'habitation Monde-Uni a lot at 7965, boulevard de l'Acadie, where 26 housing units are to be built.

The City signs two funding agreements with the Société d'habitation du Québec for temporary housing and housing search assistance. It adds $877,312 to its assistance to Mission Unitaînés for a 100-unit building for seniors and grants $581,845 to the Coopérative d'habitation Monde-Uni for the Acadie project.

Following a public consultation meeting held on February 26, 2026, city council amends the by-law on social, affordable and family housing: it will now only apply to projects larger than 18,000 square metres and will require 20% non-market housing. Ahuntsic-Cartierville amends its by-law on fees for temporary occupancy of public property related to social and affordable housing projects.

etapes.titre: Purchase of a lot in Le Sud-Ouest
etapes.texte: The City purchases, for $9,293,113, a vacant 1,535.1 square-metre lot east of rue Chatham and north of rue William, for social housing purposes. It also removes eleven lots in Ville-Marie and Le Sud-Ouest from the list of properties subject to the right of first refusal for social housing.

etapes.titre: 350 housing units at Angus, 72 housing units in Rosemont
etapes.texte: The City grants $25,110,800 to the Société du Patrimoine Angus Résidentiel to build 350 affordable housing units at the Technopôle Angus. The executive committee authorizes the SHDM to build a 72-unit building on the "Solotech" lot, on 2e Avenue.

aSurveiller.texte: Deadline for the sale of the lot at rue Chatham and rue William: August 12, 2026.
SHDM project on 2e Avenue: public call for tenders in late summer or early fall 2026, construction start by the end of 2026, delivery in May 2028.
Affordable housing units at Technopôle Angus: occupancy expected by April 30, 2027 at the latest.
Construction sites announced by the SHDM: De Maisonneuve in Ville-Marie in spring 2026, Jardin des Prairies in fall 2026, and a 72-unit project at the corner of Gilford and 2e Avenue in fall 2026.

louvain-est.description: The neighbourhood being built on municipal land in Ahuntsic-Cartierville: acquisitions, soil decontamination, street names, transitional developments.

etapes.texte: City council amended two leases for lots south of rue de Louvain and west of boulevard Saint-Laurent: a 2,787-square-metre lot leased to the Société de transport de Montréal for $49,293 in total, and an 836-square-metre lot leased to a paid parking company for $45,049 before taxes.

etapes.titre: Loans of lots for temporary uses
etapes.texte: The City is extending, free of charge, the loan of a 10,000-square-foot lot to an organization that grows a vegetable garden there, and of a 3,316-square-metre lot to an urban agriculture organization for sunflowers and a greenhouse. City council also agreed to prepare itself a free lease of 78,244 square feet, at the southeast corner of rue de Louvain Ouest and avenue de l'Esplanade, for animation activities.

etapes.titre: Contract to redevelop rue de Louvain
etapes.texte: The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension awarded a company the redevelopment of rue de Louvain between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum of $8,199,514.82 taxes included, and authorized a total expenditure of $11,192,464.62. The work covers sewers, waterworks, lighting, traffic lights, sidewalks, the bike path and plantings.

etapes.titre: The central street gets a name
etapes.texte: City council named the new street at the heart of the ecoquartier "avenue des Solidarités." The name comes from a public call for proposals held in fall 2024.

etapes.titre: Animation and events on the site
etapes.texte: The borough granted $35,000 to an organization to design and run the Esplanade-Louvain temporary space, at 150, rue de Louvain Ouest, from June 9 to December 31, 2026. It also authorized an event-based and temporary use on a vacant lot at 50 and 150, rue de Louvain Ouest: multimedia activity, shows, street food, alcohol service and recreational activities.

etapes.titre: New street, utilities and remediated soil
etapes.texte: The City awarded a company a contract of $10,311,940.25 taxes included to build a street with sewer, waterworks, roadway, lighting and soil management in the ecoquartier, for a total expenditure of $15,366,336, and added $2,007,312.15 net to remediate the soil of the former gas station area. The borough also adopted a second draft resolution authorizing the demolition of a building at avenue de l'Esplanade and rue de Louvain Ouest and the construction of a group of buildings.

aSurveiller.texte: The rue de Louvain worksite between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel is taking place in three phases: May to November 2026, May to October 2027, then May to August 2028.
The loan of the lot for sunflowers and the greenhouse runs from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2027.
The lease for animation activities covers two periods from April 1 to October 31, in 2026 and 2027.
Four other public spaces on the site remain to be named by the end of the development, expected around 2032.
The parking lease with the Société de transport de Montréal starts on October 1, 2026, for three years and a maximum of 92 days per year.

matieres-residuelles.description: Collections, sorting centres, biomethanation and ecocentres.
matieres-residuelles.enBref: The City changed collection schedules and frequencies in several boroughs, and extended contracts for food waste treatment, container collection, and container transport for the écocentre Saint-Laurent. It also purchased collection bins, awarded companies hydro-excavation work with waste material treatment, and received the 2025 waste management reports.

etapes.titre: Extensions of collection and treatment contracts
etapes.texte: The City extended two contracts with Recyclage Notre-Dame inc. by six months to treat food waste, with an additional expenditure of $3,269,055.43 including taxes [CG26 0045]. It also extended by 12 months the contracts for garbage collection in front-loading and semi-underground containers, and the contract for supplying and transporting containers for the écocentre Saint-Laurent.

The executive committee changed the collection days, schedules and sectors in L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève, Le Plateau-Mont-Royal and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve. In Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, garbage is collected every two weeks from November 1 to April 30 and every week from May 1 to October 31 [CE26 0466].

The City entered into agreements with USD Global inc., Orbis Canada ltée and Plasti-Bac inc. to supply and distribute collection bins for residents. Ahuntsic-Cartierville retained Ville en vert to inform and raise awareness among residents of buildings of eight units or fewer in the Ahuntsic and Sault-au-Récollet districts, where the frequency of garbage collection is being changed, for $230,108.67 including taxes [CA26 09 0141].

Le Plateau-Mont-Royal authorized the removal of two dwelling units in the basement of 397, boulevard Saint-Joseph Ouest to set up a waste storage room of at least 28 m² and 32 bicycle spaces. Le Sud-Ouest lifted the requirement to set up a drop-off area on the site of the future building at 2380, rue Notre-Dame Ouest, and the executive committee approved an agreement with Tricentris, which is paying $43,773.61 for a reusable dish, water fountain and sorting station loan program.

The urban agglomeration council took note of the 2025 waste management report and the accountability report for the 2020-2025 Master Plan: 415 kg of waste per person, 48% of materials diverted from disposal, and 29 of 49 actions completed [CG26 0311]. Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles, Saint-Laurent and Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce filed their expenditure reports for the activities delegated to them.

aSurveiller.texte: The extension of the food waste treatment contracts runs until September 30, 2026.
The container collection contracts and the écocentre Saint-Laurent container contract are maintained until October 31, 2027.
The reusable dish, water fountain and sorting station loan program is offered until December 31, 2026 at the latest.
The hydro-excavation contracts end on December 31, 2028.

namur-hippodrome.description: The new district on the site of the former Blue Bonnets racetrack: sale of land, loan by-laws, water main in the Namur–De la Savane sector.

etapes.titre: More time to sell a piece of land
etapes.texte: The Gouvernement du Québec grants the City an extension until October 31, 2027 to sell a first piece of land on the site, west of boulevard Décarie and south of rue Paré. The extension does not involve any financial compensation, and the other conditions of the 2017 transfer remain the same.

The City guarantees a $2,000,000 loan from the Canada Infrastructure Bank to Société GALOPH, a non-profit organization, to pay for feasibility studies for the residential project. The same day, city council rejects a motion from the Official Opposition on governance and management of public assets in the district.

City council adopts a $29,000,000 loan by-law for soil remediation, sewers and water mains, street redevelopment, professional fees and land purchases. This work must service the first lots of phase 1, intended for social, community and affordable housing.

A second loan by-law, for $12,000,000, funds the construction of main water lines between boulevard Cavendish, in Saint-Laurent, and rue Isabella, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce. It covers plans and specifications, soil studies, surveying, decontamination, land purchases and a first batch of work.

aSurveiller.texte: October 31, 2027: deadline granted by the Gouvernement du Québec to sell a first piece of land on the site.
2031: the $128.3M federal grant is conditional on the infrastructure being completed by this date.

parcs.description: Development and redevelopment of parks, including the Grand parc de l'Ouest.
parcs.enBref: The City is having parks redone all across its territory: play areas, water play features, trails, sports fields and dog parks. It is awarding design and construction contracts, adjusting contracts already underway, and paying for the decontamination of sites where parks will be developed. In the Grand parc de l'Ouest, it is repairing structures, submitting a bid for an international designation, and adding an area to the registry of protected natural environments.

etapes.texte: The City is awarding the winning team of an architecture competition the design of the Caroline-Dawson library and the redevelopment of parc Le Prévost, in Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, for a total expenditure of $10,559,257.81, taxes included. It is also paying $174,471.56 to Verdun for soil studies before redoing the play areas of parc Monseigneur-J.-A.-Richard, which was built on a former dump.

etapes.titre: Work and protection at the Grand parc de l'Ouest
etapes.texte: The City is adding $162,897.98 to the contract to repair the heritage walls on chemin de Senneville and is awarding a contract to rebuild a culvert under that same road, in the Bois-de-la-Roche agricultural hub. It is submitting the bid for the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector for the Urban Night Sky Place designation and adding the Anse-à-l'Orme sector to the registry of protected natural environments.

The boroughs are awarding contracts to redo parks: the Lucie-Bruneau dog park in Anjou, parc Mackenzie-King in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, the Alexis-Nihon dog park in Saint-Laurent, parc Monseigneur-Langlois in Verdun, and parc Percy-Walters in Ville-Marie. Outremont is paying $150,000 to redo the play module at the parc-école Saint-Germain.

City council is transferring a 810.2 m² section of the former rue Eadie to parc Campbell Ouest, in the Sud-Ouest. Le Plateau-Mont-Royal is awarding a construction contract for parc Denise-Morelle and paying an additional amount to the project's architects, while LaSalle is awarding the redevelopment of parc J.O.R.-Leduc.

aSurveiller.texte: Parc des Eaux-Cachées public art competition: winner chosen in October 2026, contract in December 2026, artwork installed in 2028.
Urban Night Sky Place bid: lighting plan submitted in February 2027, response from DarkSky expected in April 2027, site brought into compliance in April 2032.
Parc du Bassin-à-Bois: final acceptance of the work expected in June 2027.
Parc Denise-Morelle: work from early August 2026 to November 2026.
Parc J.O.R.-Leduc: work from August 2026 to June 2028.
Parc Percy-Walters: work from July to November 2026, with a follow-up in spring 2027.

pietonnisation.description: Pedestrian streets, public squares and business promotion by-laws.
pietonnisation.enBref: This year, the City and the boroughs are organizing the pedestrian streets for summer 2026: funding for boroughs and business development corporations, then by-laws that close streets to cars and set rules for terraces, sales, music and signage. Temporary public squares are also being set up, and support services are being added, such as on-demand transportation on avenue du Mont-Royal.

etapes.titre: Grant framework and end of a legal dispute
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie adopts a by-law allowing it to fund its business development corporations to pedestrianize streets in 2026, up to $425 per linear metre. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie settles out of court for $41,686.46 a lawsuit related to work on the public square at the corner of rues Beaubien Est and Boyer.

The executive committee pays $2,694,500 to six boroughs for pedestrian streets on commercial arteries. Ville-Marie and Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce adopt their first by-laws, including the Placette CDN, open from April 1 to October 31, 2026.

Ville-Marie grants $375,500 to the Société de développement commercial du Village for rue Sainte-Catherine Est, and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension $102,045 for rue Villeray. Outremont sets aside $105,000 for avenue Bernard, in addition to a $106,000 grant from the Service du développement économique.

Outremont closes avenue Bernard from May 19 to September 24, 2026. Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce turns avenues Royal and Madison into pedestrian streets and public squares from June 1 to October 31, 2026. Ville-Marie adjusts the dates of three pedestrianizations.

Le Plateau-Mont-Royal bans amplified instruments and games between 9 p.m. and 8 a.m. on pedestrianized avenues. The City pays $40,000 for activities on the rue Notre-Dame Ouest pedestrian street from July 10 to 19, 2026, and Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce authorizes a business promotion on avenue de Monkland.

aSurveiller.texte: Activities on the rue Notre-Dame Ouest pedestrian street from July 10 to 19, 2026; the organization must submit its accountability report by August 31, 2026 at the latest.
Avenue de Monkland closed to traffic from August 19 at 10 p.m. to August 24 at 7 a.m., with activities from August 20 to 23, 2026.
Avenue Lacombe closed to cars from September 10 to 13, 2026.
Rue Ontario Est pedestrianized until September 18, 2026; parking meters return on September 17, 2026.
Avenue Bernard fully reopened to traffic as of September 25, 2026.
Placette CDN and avenues Royal and Madison: traffic returns after October 31, 2026, namely November 1, 2026 for the placette.

plan-urbanisme.description: The PUM and the concordance by-laws that each borough adopts to comply with it.

etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville amends its urban planning by-law for the planting, maintenance, protection and felling of trees. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie reviews its by-laws on urban planning, special projects and demolition, and Saint-Léonard does the same for its special projects and demolitions, after public consultations held on February 26 and February 11, 2026.

The borough extends its list of buildings of heritage interest, regulates lodging establishments and services for people in residential instability, and amends its by-laws on demolition, special projects and site planning and architectural integration plans. A public meeting was held on March 18, 2026, and a written consultation from March 11 to 18, 2026.

The borough changes the heights, uses and lot occupancy ratio in the sector bounded by avenue Papineau, avenue Émile-Journault, avenue André-Grasset and rue Legendre Est. It also increases the allowed heights on sections of rue Lajeunesse, between boulevard Crémazie and boulevard Henri-Bourassa.

etapes.titre: Requests for extension to the ministry
etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville asks for twelve more months, until June 16, 2027, to adopt its concordance by-laws. L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève asks for six more months, citing lack of staff, the complexity of its territory and the fall 2025 election.

Ville-Marie amends its urban planning by-law and its by-laws on special projects, demolition, authorization certificates and cadastral operations. Following the public consultation of March 25, 2026, the City reviewed the view corridor and height plans; the by-law allows a maximum height of 103 m on the block of the former terrasse Peel and requires approval for certain work in the declared heritage site of Mont-Royal.

Saint-Léonard takes note of two correction minutes signed on March 19, 2026, which correct the name of a school and the identification of a building on boulevard Provencher. Ahuntsic-Cartierville then adopts its by-law on the demolition of buildings, after a public consultation meeting held on June 23, 2026.

aSurveiller.texte: L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève indicates it wants to present its project to elected officials starting mid-June 2026 and hold a public consultation in September or October 2026.

The Minister of Municipal Affairs has set June 16, 2027 as the deadline for Saint-Léonard to adopt all its concordance by-laws; other blocks are announced, including the replacement of the zoning by-law.
Ahuntsic-Cartierville asks for an extension until June 16, 2027 to adopt its concordance by-laws.
Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension has until June 17, 2027 to update its by-laws; its zoning by-law must be replaced in 2027.

securite-publique.description: The Service de police de la Ville de Montréal: contracts, neighbourhood stations, city council motions.
securite-publique.enBref: This year, the City is funding equipment for the Service de police de la Ville de Montréal (SPVM) through a loan by-law and awarding purchase and service contracts: motorcycles, practice ammunition, meals for detained persons, and maintenance of buildings and software. It is also renewing leases for neighbourhood stations, the training centre and parking spaces, and lending police officers to the Gendarmerie royale du Canada and the Sûreté du Québec. Several borough councils adopted motions of support for the SPVM after the shooting of June 22, 2026.

etapes.titre: Vehicles, building and services for the SPVM
etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration council is buying 11 motorcycles for road patrol, replacing the oil heating at the cavalry station at 1515, chemin Remembrance, and awarding the meals for detained persons to a new supplier. It is also extending the janitorial services for headquarters and the maintenance of the call dispatch system software.

The executive committee is authorizing the SPVM to receive an $8,000 grant from the ministère de la Justice du Canada. The money funds video segments in the metro and a police kiosk during the Victims and Survivors of Crime Week, from May 11 to 15, 2026.

etapes.titre: Leases for stations and the training centre
etapes.texte: The City is renewing the leases for neighbourhood station 15, rue de l'Église in Verdun, and neighbourhood station 26, avenue Mountain Sights in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce. It is also extending the rental of the SPVM training centre, rue Ernest-Cormier in Anjou, and renting 50 parking spaces at 260, boulevard De Maisonneuve for headquarters vehicles.

aSurveiller.texte: "Fèves au lard" fundraising day at neighbourhood station 46, on October 23, 2026.
End of the heating replacement work at the cavalry station, on September 30, 2027.
The City plans to replace the SPVM's call dispatch system at the end of 2027.
New term of the training centre lease, rue Ernest-Cormier, starting November 1, 2033.

transport-collectif.description: What the City decides around the network: land sold to the STM, station surroundings, agreements.
transport-collectif.enBref: This year, the City approved the budget and capital works program of the Société de transport de Montréal (STM), then a loan by-law of the corporation. It also sold or leased land to the STM to expand metro facilities, entrusted the STM with work related to the extension of the blue line, and regulated construction sites in the metro tunnel. It also signed a letter of no objection for the reconstruction of a bridge-tunnel above the REM.

etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration council adopted the STM's 2026 budget, balanced at $1,804,314,410 in revenues and expenditures, and the 2026-2035 capital works program. The city council gave the same direction.

The City entered into a 36-month agreement with Produits Suncor Énergie for clear diesel and diesel containing renewable fuel, following a call for tenders by the STM. It also purchased, without a call for tenders, advertising space from Astral Affichage in the metro and buses for Espace pour la vie, up to $172,462.50 including taxes.

The City is leasing to the STM a 2,787 square metre plot of land in Ahuntsic-Cartierville, south of rue de Louvain, as parking for the vehicles of officers holding a permit, for a total rent of $49,293. The same borough modified bus waiting stops within its territory as part of the network overhaul.

The City signed an agreement with the STM to build a pavilion in Parc Irma-LeVasseur, adjoining the metro ventilation station on avenue Wiseman, in Outremont. It also entrusted the STM with carrying out its municipal work at the future Pie-IX and Viau stations, on rue Jean-Talon Est, for an expenditure of $3,808,451.29 including taxes.

Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce signed a new access agreement with the STM for a vacant 3,274.2 square metre plot of land at 4636-4670, boulevard Décarie, and terminated the 2024 transitional occupancy agreement. Ville-Marie authorized the STM to drill and restore the vault of the green line tunnel, between Berri-UQAM and Saint-Laurent, 24 hours a day.

aSurveiller.texte: Drilling and restoration work on the vault of the green line tunnel until July 31, 2026.
Awarding of contracts for the Pie-IX and Viau stations in August and October 2026; opening of the blue line extension stations expected in 2031.
Start of the STM's parking lease on October 1, 2026, for three years, at a rate of 92 days per year.
Work on the Rielle ventilation station, in Verdun, until December 2027.
Complete closure of rue Wilderton, for a maximum of two weeks, during the 2027 summer holidays; reconstruction work on the bridge-tunnel from June 2026 to March 2028.

velo.titre: Cycling: REV, bike paths and BIXI
velo.description: The Réseau express vélo, bike paths and bike lanes, and the BIXI bike-share system.
velo.enBref: This year, the City is buying bikes, docking points and station parts for the BIXI system, and having new stations installed at street construction sites. It is also funding the repair of existing bike paths, including the REV Lajeunesse, and regularizing the rents on Hydro-Québec land crossed by bike paths. Boroughs, for their part, oversee the development and maintenance of their own bike paths.

etapes.texte: Outremont authorizes an expenditure of $100,000, taxes included, for concrete, de-icing salt and abrasives intended notably for bike paths. Ahuntsic-Cartierville awards Déneigement et Excavation M. Gauthier inc. the rental of a mini sweeper with operator for the spring cleaning of paths less than 1.8 metres wide, for $153,395.05, taxes included.

etapes.titre: Sustainable mobility corridors in the east
etapes.texte: City council adds $3,400,000, taxes included, to the contract with Bruneau Électrique inc. for traffic lights, civil and electrical work and bike paths in Ville-Marie and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, on rue Hochelaga and rue du Havre. The contract reaches $11,399,999.99, taxes included.

City council approves a $125,167.62 agreement, taxes included, with Hydro-Québec for rents from 2014 to 2025 on 19 lots used for bike paths, parks and community gardens. It then approves a 10-year lease, for a total rent of $46,896, taxes included, to rent about 366 square metres in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles for bike path purposes.

etapes.titre: Repair of the REV Lajeunesse and rue Lajoie
etapes.texte: Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension offers to take charge of repairing sections of the REV Lajeunesse, between rue Jarry and boulevard Crémazie, and city council accepts this offer as well as Ville-Marie's offer for roadway and bike path work under the 2019 Bike Plan. Outremont tables a draft by-law to convert the shared lane on avenue Lajoie, between Stuart and Outremont, into a one-way bike path.

aSurveiller.texte: For the REV Lajeunesse, the file indicates a call for tenders in May 2026, contract awards in June and work from July to August 2026.
The UCI Road World Championships are held in Montréal from September 20 to 27, 2026; sections along the route are targeted by roadway work in Ville-Marie.
The repair of the bike path on rue De Louvain, between west of rue d'Iberville and boulevard Saint-Michel, is scheduled at $570,000 in 2027.
The sustainable mobility corridors construction site resumes in spring 2026, for completion in spring or summer 2026.
